stocks_to_avoid.reason: CoreWeave exhibits extreme financial stress and unsustainable leverage. The company has a 1,000% debt-to-equity ratio with $45 billion in net debt and negative free cash flows. While revenue and backlog keep the stock price afloat, the company requires $35 billion in additional financing just to fulfill existing commitments (not including new business). CoreWeave's bond yields spiked to 15%, the highest ever, and credit default swap insurance costs reached unprecedented levels. The creator explicitly warns this represents a 'house of cards' structure where the company is taking on more debt than it can afford to pay, subject to credit events if yields continue rising regardless of underlying demand fundamentals.
stocks_to_avoid.risk: Credit default risk; potential 50-90% downside if financing becomes unavailable or debt must be restructured.

stocks_to_avoid.reason: Anthropic is seeking a $60 billion debt package and offering Blackstone yields above 10%, which is junk bond territory for a company that hasn't even gone public yet. The creator considers this a major red flag. Additionally, the market reacted negatively when Anthropic reported $16.8 billion in Q3 revenue (up from $11.6 billion), interpreting the quarter-over-quarter growth deceleration as disappointing despite the absolute growth. Like CoreWeave, Anthropic is part of the problematic pattern of AI companies taking on unsustainable leverage to fund operations and meet backlog obligations.
stocks_to_avoid.risk: IPO launch risk; debt burden may impair valuation and dilute equity; company growth may not support debt service if capex spending slows.

key_warnings: DATA CENTER FINANCING BUBBLE: Companies like CoreWeave, Iron, and Nebus have astronomical and 'fantastical' loan amounts that create systemic risk. The creator identifies this as the one part of the AI boom that is genuinely uncomfortable, warning that when macroeconomic yields go against these highly leveraged companies, credit events can occur independent of company fundamentals or demand. This applies to CoreWeave, Anthropic, OpenAI, and hyperscalers taking on massive debt to fund AI capex.

HOT INFLATION AND DECEMBER RATE HIKE RISK: CPI came in at 3.7% vs 3.6% expected, up from 3.4%. PPI was worse than expected at +1.3% monthly (biggest jump since March 2022 vs 0.6% estimate). The market is pricing in a 77% probability of a rate hike in December 2024, up from previous expectations of a hold. This reignites fears of Fed tightening and could trigger significant equity selloffs if inflation surprises remain hot.

ARTIFICIAL MEMORY PRICING AND CHINESE COMPETITION: Memory stocks (Korean indices, SOXL) are under pressure from Chinese memory competition, creating a 'DeepSeek moment for memory.' While the creator dismisses this partly as FUD, JP Morgan still projects 20% memory shortages this year and 19% next year, so structural support remains. However, Chinese competition could pressure pricing and margins.

HEDGE FUND BLOWUP RISK: Rumors of hedge fund blowups were circulating, with confirmed mass liquidations of AI positions in one week (nearly 2 years of net AI buying unwound). If this spreads to larger hedge funds or causes cascading margin calls, it could trigger broader market selloffs.

HIGH YIELD SPREADS WIDENING: High yield spreads are rising, though not yet at the 3.5% level where the creator would become seriously worried. However, any further widening past 3.5% combined with rising yields could signal credit stress contagion into investment-grade securities.

YIELD TRAJECTORY RISK: The 10-year yield briefly broke above 5.3% (2007 highs) before pulling back below 5%. If yields break back above 5.3%, it would signal risk-off conditions. However, the creator notes the 2018 pattern (Trump's midterm year) where yields topped in October before declining, suggesting yields may have peaked.

CAPEX COMMITMENT UNCERTAINTY: If hyperscalers (Meta, Google, Amazon, Microsoft) signal capex cuts for 2027 despite current $750 billion spending plans, this would be 'bad for overall AI' and could trigger a 'market crashing event.' Mega cap earnings (Oct 20-Nov 17) are critical to validate continued capex commitment.

MIDTERM YEAR SEASONALITY: This is a midterm election year with historical patterns of September-October volatility. October is typically the best performing month in midterm years, but this year has shown weakness. The creator acknowledges the seasonal pattern is similar to 2018 (Trump's midterm) with potential for more downside before recovery.

OPEX TECHNICAL LEVEL: Historical analysis of 44 OPEX dates shows that OPEX lows are typically retested within a week or less when OPEX is a red day (as October 18 was). This suggests QQQ and tech could drop further before establishing a lasting bottom.

CREDIT EVENT SPREADING RISK: Although not yet evidenced in investment-grade spreads, if credit stress from data center companies spreads to the broader high yield and investment grade markets, it could rapidly become a systemic issue. The creator is monitoring this closely.
